transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-31 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Carlos (Redwood SA), Michael (CTO - Pinecrest), Lina (Head of ML), Rahul (Infra), Adele (Product)

Summary: Short POC scoping to align on success criteria, workload sizing and benchmark approach to decide between Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment. Pinecrest wants cost/latency tradeoffs, security checklist (VPC/KMS/SOC2) and a 2-week benchmark plan.

Topics covered: success metrics, p95 latency goals, QPS, token distribution, canary/rollout, security controls, pilot timeline

00:00 Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, let's do quick intros and then go into what you're trying to validate in the POC
00:17 Michael (Pinecrest): yeah thanks, I'm Michael, CTO. Our main question is, can we run our routing + summarization pipeline at p95 < 200ms for 256-token prompts at 200 concurrent users, and keep cost predictable. We're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private, and need a concrete benchmark plan.
00:45 Priya (Redwood SE): quick q, when you say 200 concurrent users is that web concurrency or backend workers?
:53 Michael: web concurrency hitting the API, roughly 200 sustained for peak 30 minute windows.
01:10 Lina (Pinecrest): and token mix — ~70% short (<=64 tokens), 20% medium (65-256), 10% long (>256). Also embeddings for search at lower QPS but high volume (batch jobs overnight).
01:35 Rahul (Infra): on security — we need SOC 2, SSO (SAML), KMS integration for keys, and VPC peering or an on-prem option for regulated clients. Do you support audit logs?
01:50 Jordan: yes, Redwood has audit logs, SOC 2, SAML; for private deployments we do customer-controlled KMS and on-prem bundles. We'll share the security doc link after the call.
02:15 Carlos (Redwood SA): to frame the decision, hosted gives fastest time-to-value, dedicated locks in capacity and more predictable unit economics, private/VPC gives isolation+KMS control but higher ops overhead. We'll propose a 2-week benchmark across two modes.

02:45 Michael: what does a 2-week benchmark look like? we can't test everything.
03:00 Priya: pragmatic plan: (a) synthetic replay from your traces for latency/throughput; (b) token-length distribution tests; (c) tail latency / cold-start / cache hit tests; (d) qualitative eval for output drift. For hosted vs dedicated we can run identical workloads and measure p50/p95/p99, token cost, and bytes/sec.
03:30 Adele (Product): timeline question — if dedicated looks better, how fast can Redwood provision dedicated for a pilot?
03:42 Carlos: typical lead time for a small dedicated pool is 7-14 days after contract/ordering, depending on GPU availability. For a pilot we often do a shorter reserved test with burst capacity.

04:05 Michael: we're sensitive to cost — do you have sample unit economics for 8k vs 16k context windows and quantized models?
04:22 Jordan: we'll send a cost model spreadsheet, but high-level — dedicated reduces per-token cost at scale because of fixed pool amortization, hosted is simpler but hits higher unit costs for sustained throughput. Quantization and batching are big levers.

04:50 Lina: about batching and latency — our UX needs <200ms p95, but some ops are async. How much does batching add to tail?
05:05 Priya: batching can increase latency if you wait too long to fill a batch. Redwood runtime supports dynamic batching with latency SLOs so we prioritize low latency for pinned routes, and enable larger batches on background jobs. We can set per-route policies.
05:35 Michael: can you guarantee fallback if Dedicated capacity saturates?
05:44 Carlos: yes, routing policies can fail over to hosted-compatible model variants or lower-cost instances. You can do canary and automatic fallback. There are also QoS knobs for rate-limiting.

06:10 Rahul: on the private option — what's the difference between VPC/provider-managed and on-prem on patching, upgrades?
06:25 Jordan: VPC private deployment uses our control plane but seats in your VPC; we manage runtime upgrades through scheduled windows. On-prem (air-gapped) is a different deliverable — you manage infra and we provide packages. Patching cadence is coordinated.

06:55 Lina: any compliance gotchas for EU data residency? we have customers in EU wanting data to never leave region.
07:05 Carlos: we support region pinning for hosted; Dedicated can be provisioned in EU regions; Private deployed in-region ensures data residency. We'll note any cross-border telemetry in the SOC doc.

07:40 Michael: ok benchmark specifics, we can provide 14 days of production traces anonymized, is that enough?
07:52 Priya: yes, a sample is fine — we'll do a replay with the same inter-arrival times, plus synthetic spikes. We'll also seed prompt sets for quality checks.
08:12 Adele: what success criteria should we agree on?
08:20 Jordan: propose primary success metrics: p95 generation latency <200ms for 256 tokens, throughput >=200 concurrent with <5% error rate, cost per 1M tokens under X (we'll calculate), and no security blockers for SOC2/SAML/KMS. Secondary: embedding latency for batch jobs <500ms per item, model output quality within acceptable deviation vs current baseline.

08:55 Michael: we need clarity on what you mean by 'cost per 1M tokens under X' — please put numbers in spreadsheet.
09:05 Jordan: yep will put ranges based on hosted vs dedicated assumptions.

09:18 Priya: technical benchmark steps (high level): 1) ingest traces + split traffic; 2) run hosted baseline (small sample); 3) run Dedicated pilot (same workload); 4) run Private if requested; 5) compare metrics + regression tests. We'll instrument KV cache hit-rates, batching behavior, and GPU utilization.
09:50 Rahul: about KV cache — is that local GPU memory or external? we care about cache warm-up times for repeated prompts.
10:02 Priya: Redwood has both in-runtime KV cache and optional external cache layers; warm-up matters, so we'll measure cold vs warm p95s. Sometimes transcripts say KV cash, haha, but it's cache.
10:22 Michael: any suggested model families or quantization for our use-case? we currently use a 13B family model with FP16 on prem.
10:32 Priya: for low-latency with similar quality, a quantized 13B or 7B may work; we'll recommend model variants after initial perf runs. Sometimes smaller models can hit your latency SLO with acceptable quality.

11:00 Adele: who will own the pilot on Redwood side and Pinecrest side? we need clear owners.
11:10 Jordan: Redwood owner is Jordan (AE) for commercial, Priya is SE lead, Carlos for architecture. Pinecrest owners?
11:20 Michael: Michael (CTO) owner, Rahul infra lead, Lina for ML quality, Adele product.

11:35 Priya: let's walk through an example micro-benchmark quickly — 256-token prompt, 200 concurrent, 50 RPS sustained, 2000 RPS spike tests for 30s. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU util, batch sizes, and token cost.
11:58 Rahul: for the 200 concurrent 256-token case, can you share expected GPU counts for Dedicated?
12:12 Carlos: preliminary estimate: for a 13B quantized model with optimized kernels, maybe 4-6 A10-ish GPUs for sustained 200 concurrency depending on batching and dynamic batching behavior; we'll provide a more detailed sizing once we see traces.
12:40 Michael: price sensitivity again — we need to compare three scenarios: hosted for 6 months, dedicated for pilot (1 month reserved), private (on-prem) with ops overhead.
12:58 Jordan: we'll build that comparison — hypothesis: dedicated pilot will reduce per-token cost by ~25-45% vs hosted at your sustained throughput; private may have similar or slightly better unit cost but significant ops & capex.

13:20 Adele: paperwork timelines — procurement and legal will want the security pack, SLAs, and a one-page pilot SOW. Can you provide a short SOW for the 2-week benchmark?
13:33 Jordan: yes, we'll draft a 2-week pilot SOW with scope, acceptance criteria, rollback/fallback, and pricing options.

13:55 Michael: sample artifacts you said you'd share?
14:00 Jordan: hosting comparison spreadsheet, security compliance pack (SOC2, SAML doc, KMS guide), and a link to a lightweight benchmark harness repo — we'll post links in the follow-up email. We'll also add an example JMeter/locust script for the replay.

14:28 Priya: quick note on evaluation: include quality checks using a subset of prompts and human-eval or automated similarity metric; we'll run side-by-side to flag regressions.
14:45 Lina: yes we'll provide quality baselines and key prompts.

15:05 Rahul: can we do a short smoke test on hosted first while we prep traces? to make sure instrumentation works.
15:12 Carlos: absolutely, we typically do a hosted smoke-run within 48h of receiving sample traces.

15:35 Jordan: recap and next steps: Jordan share spreadsheet + SOW draft by 2026-04-02; Priya share initial benchmark harness by 2026-04-07; Michael provide traces & SLOs by 2026-04-04; schedule kickoff for 2026-04-05. Any other blockers?
15:58 Michael: none from me, thanks. Great call.

16:10 End of call.
